name: Barbell Bench Press
specificInstructions: Set the rack safeties just below chest height or use a spotter; lie with your eyes below the bar and both feet flat on the floor.
Draw your shoulder blades back against the bench, grip slightly wider than shoulder-width, and unrack with your wrists stacked over your forearms.
Bend your elbows to lower the bar toward your lower-to-mid chest, keeping your forearms approximately vertical and your upper arms about 45-60 degrees from your torso.
Press upward and slightly back toward your shoulders while keeping your head, upper back, and buttocks on the bench; straighten your elbows without bouncing the bar.
coachTip: Plant your paws! Steady feet and a quiet upper back make a much stronger launchpad.

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
specificInstructions: Set an incline bench around 30 degrees inside a rack with safeties or a spotter, and plant your feet with your upper back supported.
Retract your shoulder blades, take a grip slightly wider than your shoulders, and lift the bar above your upper chest.
Lower toward the upper chest below the collarbones while keeping your wrists above your elbows and your shoulders against the pad.
Press the bar upward over your shoulders without lifting your hips or forcing an exaggerated arch through your lower back.
coachTip: A small hill is enough, fox friend. Keep the incline modest so your upper chest stays in the game.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
specificInstructions: Sit with the dumbbells supported on your thighs, then lie back and bring them beside your chest with your feet firmly grounded.
Keep your shoulder blades against the bench and position each wrist over its elbow, with your upper arms angled slightly inward from your shoulders.
Press both weights above your chest, bringing them slightly toward each other without clashing them together.
Lower until your upper arms are approximately level with your torso, or stop sooner if your shoulders cannot stay comfortably controlled.
coachTip: Two paws, one smooth rhythm. Let both weights arrive together without a noisy dumbbell high-five.

name: Incline Dumbbell Bench Press
specificInstructions: Set the bench to roughly 30 degrees, sit with dumbbells on your thighs, and guide them beside your upper chest as you lean back.
Keep your feet down, your shoulder blades supported, and your wrists above your elbows rather than letting the weights tip backward.
Press upward over your shoulders while keeping your ribs from lifting away from your pelvis.
Lower the weights toward the sides of your upper chest until your upper arms reach a comfortable depth; reverse without bouncing.
coachTip: Keep your ribs tucked like a cozy fox curl. The chest should press, not your lower back.

name: Dumbbell Chest Fly
specificInstructions: Lie on a flat bench with light dumbbells held above your chest, palms facing each other and elbows softly bent.
Keep the bend in your elbows nearly constant as you open your arms outward in a wide arc.
Stop when your upper arms are approximately level with your torso or earlier if you feel strain at the front of your shoulders.
Bring the weights back above your chest by drawing your upper arms inward; avoid turning the return into a bent-elbow press.
coachTip: Imagine hugging a big fluffy tree. A gentle elbow bend and light weights keep this hug friendly.

name: Standing Cable Chest Fly
specificInstructions: Place both cable pulleys near shoulder height, grasp the handles, and step forward into a staggered stance.
Lean slightly forward from your ankles, brace your abdomen, and hold your upper arms out with a small bend in each elbow.
Sweep your hands together in front of your chest by bringing your upper arms inward without shrugging your shoulders.
Open your arms slowly until they align with your torso, keeping your elbow angle and trunk position steady.
coachTip: Give the air a smooth fox hug. If your whole body rocks, lighten the stack and own the arc.

name: Push-Up
specificInstructions: Place your hands slightly wider than your shoulders, extend your legs, and balance on your palms and toes.
Tighten your abdomen and glutes so your head, ribs, pelvis, and heels travel as one straight line.
Bend your elbows about 30-45 degrees away from your sides and lower your chest between your hands without letting your hips sag.
Press the floor away to straighten your elbows, allowing your shoulder blades to move naturally around your ribs at the top.
coachTip: Move like a sturdy plank, not a wiggly tail! An elevated version is a great way to build clean reps.

name: Incline Push-Up
specificInstructions: Set your hands on a fixed bench or rail slightly wider than shoulder-width and walk your feet back until your body forms a straight line.
Brace your abdomen and keep your chest aligned over the space between your hands.
Bend your elbows diagonally back to bring your lower chest toward the support while keeping your hips level.
Push the support away until your elbows straighten; use a higher surface if you cannot maintain your trunk position.
coachTip: Raise the trail, keep the challenge. A higher support helps you collect strong, tidy reps.

name: Machine Chest Press
specificInstructions: Adjust the seat so the handles line up near the middle of your chest and your feet rest flat on the floor.
Sit against the back pad, grasp the handles, and keep your wrists straight with your elbows slightly below shoulder level.
Press forward by extending your elbows while keeping your shoulders and upper back against the support.
Return the handles slowly until your upper arms reach a comfortable position beside your torso; do not let the stack slam.
coachTip: Let the seat be your den wall: stay supported and make the weight stack whisper on the way home.

name: Pec Deck Fly
specificInstructions: Set the seat so the handles or elbow pads align with your chest and your shoulders remain comfortably below the machine pivots.
Place your back against the pad and grasp the handles with a soft bend in your elbows, or rest your forearms on the supported pads.
Bring your upper arms together in front of your chest while keeping your shoulders from rolling forward.
Return slowly until your arms are roughly in line with your torso, keeping a gentle bend in your elbows and tension through your chest.
coachTip: Close the den doors gently. You only need a comfortable stretch, not the widest opening the machine allows.

name: Decline Push-Up
specificInstructions: Place your toes on a stable low bench and your hands on the floor slightly wider than your shoulders.
Brace your abdomen and glutes so your head, trunk, and legs stay aligned without your lower back sagging.
Bend your elbows diagonally backward to lower your upper chest between your hands while keeping your hips steady.
Press the floor away until your elbows straighten; reduce the bench height if you cannot control the whole descent.
coachTip: A small hill adds plenty of challenge. Keep your tail level before choosing a taller perch.

name: Kneeling Push-Up
specificInstructions: Kneel on a padded floor and walk your hands forward until your body forms a straight line from your head to your knees.
Place your hands just wider than shoulder-width and tighten your abdomen without folding at your hips.
Bend your elbows about 30-45 degrees from your sides and lower your chest toward the space between your hands.
Push through both palms to straighten your arms, moving your hips and shoulders upward together.
coachTip: Knees down, quality up. Move as one sturdy little bridge and collect those confident reps.

name: Decline Dumbbell Bench Press
specificInstructions: Secure your legs on a mildly declined bench and have a partner help position the dumbbells if getting into place is awkward.
Hold the weights beside your lower chest with shoulder blades supported and wrists stacked above your elbows.
Press the dumbbells above your chest while keeping your elbows angled inward rather than flaring directly sideways.
Lower slowly until your upper arms reach a comfortable depth beside your torso, then finish by safely handing off or securing the weights.
coachTip: Get cozy and secure before you press. A safe way in and out is part of every strong set.

name: Smith Machine Bench Press
specificInstructions: Position a flat bench so the Smith bar lowers toward your mid-chest and set the safety stops just below that position.
Plant your feet, retract your shoulder blades, and take a grip that keeps your forearms nearly vertical at the bottom.
Rotate the bar off its hooks and lower it under control, keeping your elbows diagonally below your shoulders.
Press along the machine track without lifting your hips, then fully engage both hooks before releasing your grip.
coachTip: Check the trail before the lift. Bench placement and both safety hooks deserve a quick fox inspection.

name: Resistance Band Bench Press
specificInstructions: Inspect the band and secure its middle beneath a stable bench so equal lengths reach each hand without rubbing on sharp edges.
Lie on the bench with feet planted and hold the handles beside your chest with wrists straight.
Press the handles upward above your chest while keeping your shoulders supported and your forearms aligned with the pull.
Bend your elbows to return slowly, maintaining a secure grip as the band tension decreases.
coachTip: Stretchy gear still needs a sturdy den. Check the anchor and let the band return slowly.

name: Standing Chest and Shoulder Stretch
specificInstructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and clasp your hands behind your hips, using a loose towel between your hands if needed.
Gently straighten your elbows and move your hands slightly away from your pelvis without forcing the shoulder joints.
Keep your ribs down and chin level while you feel a mild stretch across your chest and the fronts of your shoulders.
Breathe slowly through the hold, then soften your elbows and release your hands without bouncing.
coachTip: Open your chest like a sunny morning stretch. Gentle tension is enough; no tug-of-war with your shoulders.

name: Lat Pulldown
specificInstructions: Secure your thighs beneath the pad and take an overhand grip on the bar slightly wider than your shoulders.
Sit tall with a small backward lean from your hips and keep your ribs stacked over your pelvis.
Drive your elbows down toward your sides to bring the bar in front of your face toward your upper chest.
Extend your elbows slowly and let your shoulder blades rotate upward as the bar rises; keep the return controlled without swinging your torso.
coachTip: Think elbows toward your back pockets. Your paws hold the bar, but your back leads the journey.

name: Pull-Up
specificInstructions: Take an overhand grip on a secure bar just wider than shoulder-width and hang with your legs clear of the floor.
Brace your abdomen, keep your legs quiet, and begin by drawing your shoulder blades down as your elbows start bending.
Pull your elbows toward your ribs until your chin clears the bar without craning your neck or kicking your legs.
Lower under control until your elbows straighten through your comfortable overhead range; use assistance if you cannot control the descent.
coachTip: Climb with quiet paws and a quiet tail. A controlled assisted rep beats a big swinging shortcut.

name: Chin-Up
specificInstructions: Grip a fixed overhead bar with palms facing you and hands approximately shoulder-width apart.
Keep your ribs down and legs still as you start pulling your elbows toward the sides of your rib cage.
Lift until your chin passes the bar while keeping your neck in line with your spine rather than reaching your chin forward.
Lower slowly to straight elbows within your comfortable shoulder range, keeping your body from swinging between repetitions.
coachTip: Let your elbows lead the climb. Your chin gets the view, but your arms and back do the hiking.

name: Seated Cable Row
specificInstructions: Sit facing a low pulley, place your feet securely on the supports, and hold the handle with your knees slightly bent.
Set your torso upright, keep your spine long, and allow your arms to reach forward without collapsing your lower back.
Pull the handle toward your lower ribs by driving your elbows backward and drawing your shoulder blades toward each other.
Extend your arms slowly and allow your shoulder blades to glide forward while your torso remains nearly still.
coachTip: Row the handle, not the whole boat. Keep your torso calm and let your elbows do the paddling.

name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
specificInstructions: Hold the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than your legs, soften your knees, and hinge your hips backward.
Keep your back neutral and your torso angled toward the floor, with the bar hanging below your shoulders.
Pull the bar toward your lower ribs by bending your elbows behind you without lifting your torso to meet it.
Lower to straight arms while maintaining your hip hinge and abdominal brace; reset if your lower-back position changes.
coachTip: Freeze your fox silhouette. If every pull turns into a little standing-up dance, reduce the load.

name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row
specificInstructions: Stand with feet about hip-width apart and a dumbbell in each hand, then bend your knees slightly and hinge at your hips.
Hold your torso steady with your spine neutral and let both weights hang beneath your shoulders with palms facing inward.
Draw your elbows back toward your hips to bring the dumbbells beside your lower ribs without rotating or jerking your trunk.
Lower the weights to straight arms while keeping your hips back and your neck aligned with your spine.
coachTip: Keep both paws on the same trail. Smooth, matching rows make your back work harder than momentum does.

name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
specificInstructions: Set a bench at a moderate incline and lie face down with your chest against the pad and feet securely on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms hanging toward the floor and your neck aligned with your upper back.
Pull your elbows behind your torso to bring the weights toward the sides of your ribs while keeping your chest against the pad.
Lower the weights slowly, allowing your shoulder blades to separate without lifting your chest to gain extra range.
coachTip: Let the bench give your chest a fox hug. Staying supported makes it easier to feel your back doing the work.

name: Straight-Arm Cable Pulldown
specificInstructions: Attach a straight bar to a high pulley, grip it overhand, and step back with your knees soft and hips slightly hinged.
Start with your arms angled above shoulder height and elbows softly bent, keeping your ribs from flaring upward.
Sweep the bar toward the fronts of your thighs by moving your upper arms down while keeping the elbow bend almost unchanged.
Return the bar slowly overhead until you feel a comfortable stretch along your sides without arching your lower back.
coachTip: Sweep your paws down like brushing tall grass. Keep your elbows quiet so your lats stay in charge.

name: Machine Seated Row
specificInstructions: Adjust the seat and chest pad so you can reach the handles with straight arms while keeping your feet supported.
Rest your chest against the pad, grip the handles, and keep your shoulders relaxed away from your ears.
Pull the handles toward your ribs by moving your elbows backward without peeling your chest away from the support.
Return until your elbows straighten and shoulder blades glide forward, keeping control of the machine throughout the return.
coachTip: Stay close to your den wall. The chest pad is there to help your back row without a torso swing.

name: Inverted Row
specificInstructions: Secure a bar in a rack around waist height, grip it overhand, and position your body underneath with your heels on the floor.
Straighten your body from head to heels and brace your glutes and abdomen; move your feet closer to make the angle easier.
Bend your elbows and draw your chest toward the bar while keeping your hips from sagging or thrusting upward.
Lower to straight arms under control, allowing your shoulder blades to move forward while your body stays aligned.
coachTip: Make yourself a sturdy bridge. Changing your foot position is a clever way to find the right challenge.

name: Underhand Lat Pulldown
specificInstructions: Adjust the thigh pad and grasp the overhead bar with palms facing you and hands approximately shoulder-width apart.
Sit tall with a small backward lean and keep your abdomen braced so your ribs do not flare.
Pull your elbows down beside your torso to guide the bar toward the front of your upper chest.
Extend your arms slowly overhead, allowing your shoulder blades to move upward without rocking your torso.
coachTip: Bring your elbows toward your pockets. Your biceps can help, but let your back lead the pull.

name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up
specificInstructions: Grasp secure parallel handles with palms facing each other and let your legs hang clear of the floor.
Brace your abdomen and begin pulling your elbows toward your ribs without swinging your legs.
Lift until your chin reaches handle height while keeping your neck aligned instead of poking your head forward.
Lower to comfortably straight arms under control; use assistance when the descent becomes difficult to manage.
coachTip: Parallel paws, quiet tail. Smooth assisted reps are a clever stepping stone to your first full climb.

name: Bent-Knee Inverted Row
specificInstructions: Secure a bar in a rack around waist height and position your chest below it with an overhand grip.
Bend your knees and plant your feet, then lift your hips so your head, shoulders, and knees form a line.
Pull your chest toward the bar by bending your elbows and drawing your shoulder blades together without dropping your hips.
Lower to straight arms while maintaining the same bent-knee bridge position.
coachTip: A shorter bridge is a strong beginning. Keep those hips lifted and make each row feel deliberate.

name: Single-Arm Standing Band Row
specificInstructions: Secure an undamaged band to a low anchor and stand facing it with a handle in one hand and a staggered stance.
Step back until the band is taut, keeping your chest and pelvis directed toward the anchor.
Draw your working elbow behind you to bring the handle beside your lower ribs without twisting your trunk.
Extend the arm slowly while resisting the band pulling your shoulder and torso forward.
coachTip: One paw rows while the rest of you stands guard. Keep your belly button facing the anchor.

name: Barbell Shrug
specificInstructions: Stand tall holding a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip just outside your legs.
Keep your elbows straight, wrists neutral, and head aligned over your rib cage.
Lift your shoulders upward toward your ears without rolling them forward or bending your elbows.
Lower your shoulder blades slowly to their resting position while keeping the bar close to your thighs.
coachTip: Think straight up, then gently down. Your shoulders do not need to draw circles around the forest.

name: Kneeling Lat Stretch
specificInstructions: Kneel on a padded floor with your hands in front of your shoulders and knees separated comfortably.
Walk your palms forward and shift your hips back toward your heels while keeping your hands grounded.
Lengthen from your hips through your fingertips and lower your chest only until you feel a comfortable stretch along your sides.
Breathe steadily without forcing your shoulders, then walk your hands back and lift your chest to release.
coachTip: Reach your paws long and let your tail settle back. A slow breath makes this den stretch feel sweeter.

name: Barbell High-Bar Squat
specificInstructions: Set rack safeties below your intended depth, position the bar on your upper trapezius rather than your neck, and step back with a secure grip.
Set your feet about shoulder-width apart with toes slightly outward, brace your abdomen, and keep pressure through your whole foot.
Bend your knees and hips together, allowing your knees to track in the direction of your toes as you lower to a depth you can control.
Push the floor away to stand, bringing your hips and shoulders upward together without letting your knees collapse inward.
coachTip: Three points under each paw: heel, big-toe base, little-toe base. Keep the whole trail under you.

name: Dumbbell Goblet Squat
specificInstructions: Hold one dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands supporting its upper end and your elbows pointing downward.
Place your feet slightly wider than hip-width with toes gently turned out, keeping your heels and forefeet grounded.
Sit down between your hips by bending your knees and hips, keeping the weight close and your knees following your toes.
Stand by driving through your whole feet while keeping your chest and pelvis rising together.
coachTip: Carry that dumbbell like a prized acorn. Keeping it close helps you squat tall and steady.

name: 45-Degree Leg Press
specificInstructions: Sit with your back and pelvis supported, place your feet about shoulder-width on the platform, and check the machine safety stops.
Extend your legs enough to release the handles while keeping your knees softly unlocked and both feet flat against the platform.
Lower the sled by bending your knees and hips, stopping before your pelvis rolls away from the back pad or your heels lift.
Press through your whole feet to return without snapping your knees straight; re-engage the safety catches before exiting.
coachTip: Your tailbone stays in the seat! A comfortable depth with a supported pelvis beats chasing the lowest sled.

name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
specificInstructions: Begin standing with a barbell at the fronts of your thighs, hands just outside your legs and knees slightly bent.
Brace your abdomen and push your hips backward while keeping the bar close enough to skim your thighs.
Continue lowering along your shins until you feel hamstring tension and can no longer hinge without rounding your back; keep your knee bend nearly constant.
Push your feet into the floor and bring your hips forward to stand tall, stopping before you lean backward at the top.
coachTip: Send your tail toward the wall behind you. The bar follows your legs; it does not lead a dive to the floor.

name: Dumbbell Forward Lunge
specificInstructions: Stand tall holding dumbbells at your sides, with feet hip-width apart and enough clear space in front of you.
Step one foot forward onto a separate hip-width track and bend both knees, keeping the front heel grounded.
Lower until your rear knee approaches the floor and your front thigh nears parallel, or stop at a shallower controlled depth.
Push through the front foot to return to standing without twisting your pelvis, then alternate legs.
coachTip: Walk on two trails, not a tightrope. A little space between your feet makes the landing steadier.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Lunge
specificInstructions: Stand with a dumbbell beside each thigh and feet about hip-width apart, keeping your abdomen braced.
Step one foot backward and land on its forefoot while leaving the front foot planted flat.
Bend both knees to lower the rear knee toward the floor, keeping the front knee aligned with the toes and your pelvis facing forward.
Press through the front foot to bring the rear leg back under your hips, then repeat on the other side.
coachTip: The front paw is your anchor. Step back softly and let the planted leg bring you home.

name: Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat
specificInstructions: Stand a short stride in front of a stable low bench, hold dumbbells at your sides, and rest the top of one foot on the bench behind you.
Keep your front foot on its own hip-width track and distribute most of your weight through that planted foot.
Bend the front knee and hip to lower your rear knee toward the floor, keeping your pelvis level and front heel down.
Drive through the front foot to stand, using the rear leg mainly for balance; complete the set before switching sides.
coachTip: Your back paw is a kickstand, not the engine. Let the front leg earn the climb.

name: Machine Leg Extension
specificInstructions: Adjust the backrest so your knees line up with the machine pivot and place the roller just above the fronts of your ankles.
Keep your hips and back against the seat, grasp the side handles, and point your knees straight ahead.
Straighten your knees smoothly to lift the roller until your legs are nearly extended without kicking or snapping the joints.
Bend your knees slowly to return while keeping your thighs resting on the seat and the weight stack controlled.
coachTip: Lift like a fox opening a delicate gate. Smooth knee motion matters more than a big stack.

name: Lying Leg Curl
specificInstructions: Lie face down with your knees aligned to the machine pivot and the roller resting above your heels on the lower calves.
Hold the handles and keep the fronts of your hips in contact with the pad rather than arching your lower back.
Bend your knees to bring your heels toward your buttocks, stopping before your hips lift or your knees feel compressed.
Lower the roller slowly until your knees are nearly straight without letting the stack drop.
coachTip: Keep your tail resting on the pad. If your hips pop up, shorten the curl and choose a lighter load.

name: Barbell Glute Bridge
specificInstructions: Lie on your back on the floor with knees bent and feet flat, then position a padded barbell across your hip crease and steady it with both hands.
Place your feet so your shins approach vertical at the top, and gently draw your ribs toward your pelvis.
Press through your feet to lift your hips until your shoulders, hips, and knees form a line, squeezing your glutes without arching your lower back.
Lower your pelvis to the floor under control while keeping the bar centered over your hips.
coachTip: Finish with a glute squeeze, not a backbend. Your tail lifts the bridge while your ribs stay cozy.

name: Standing Machine Calf Raise
specificInstructions: Adjust the shoulder pads and place the balls of your feet on the platform with your heels free to move.
Stand tall with your abdomen braced and knees softly straight, holding the handles for balance.
Rise onto the balls of your feet by lifting your heels as high as you can without rolling your ankles outward.
Lower your heels slowly through a comfortable stretch and pause briefly before the next repetition instead of bouncing.
coachTip: Sneak up tall on your tiptoes, then lower like a quiet fox. The slow bottom pause is where control shines.

name: Seated Machine Calf Raise
specificInstructions: Sit with knees bent about 90 degrees, the thigh pads above your knees, and the balls of your feet supported on the platform.
Lift your heels enough to release the safety lever while keeping your knees beneath the pads.
Raise your heels by pressing through the balls of your feet, keeping your ankles aligned rather than rolling to their outer edges.
Lower the heels slowly to a comfortable calf stretch, then repeat without bouncing the weight or lifting your thighs from the pads.
coachTip: Tiny trail, big calf work. Keep the motion in your ankles and let the seat do the balancing.

name: Barbell Deadlift
specificInstructions: Place the bar over your midfoot with feet roughly hip-width apart, then hinge and bend your knees to grip just outside your legs.
Bring your shins near the bar, brace your abdomen, and take tension through your arms while keeping your back neutral.
Push the floor away and extend your hips and knees together, guiding the bar close to your legs until you stand tall.
Hinge your hips back first, then bend your knees as the bar passes them and settle the plates before resetting your next repetition.
coachTip: Keep the bar on your trail, close to your legs. Stand proudly at the top without leaning your tail backward.

name: Dumbbell Step-Up
specificInstructions: Stand before a fixed low box holding dumbbells beside your thighs and place one entire foot on its surface.
Lean slightly over that foot while keeping your knee aligned with your toes and your pelvis level.
Push through the elevated foot to step onto the box, minimizing the push from your trailing leg.
Lower the trailing foot slowly back to the floor and return to your starting stance before repeating.
coachTip: Choose a step your front paw can own. A lower box with a gentle landing beats a mountain-sized wobble.

name: Seated Leg Curl
specificInstructions: Adjust the seat so your knees align with the machine pivot and set the lower roller behind your ankles.
Secure the thigh pad above your knees and rest your back against the support with legs nearly extended.
Bend your knees to pull the roller downward and backward without lifting your hips off the seat.
Straighten your legs slowly to the comfortable starting range while preventing the stack from slamming.
coachTip: Keep your thighs tucked under the pad like paws under a blanket. Your knees move while your hips stay cozy.

name: Seated Hip Abduction
specificInstructions: Sit with your back supported, feet on the rests, and the pads positioned against the outsides of your knees.
Set a comfortable starting width and keep your pelvis level with your hands holding the seat handles.
Move your thighs outward against the pads without bouncing or using a forward trunk swing.
Bring your knees inward slowly until you reach the starting width, maintaining control of the resistance.
coachTip: Open the den gates smoothly. Your hips do the work while your upper body stays peacefully parked.

name: Seated Hip Adduction
specificInstructions: Sit against the backrest and position the pads on the insides of your thighs with feet supported.
Choose a starting width that gives a mild inner-thigh stretch without pulling your pelvis out of alignment.
Draw your thighs inward to bring the pads together while keeping your trunk and hips still.
Allow your knees to separate slowly back to the chosen width instead of letting the machine pull them abruptly apart.
coachTip: Close the gates with gentle strength. A comfortable starting width keeps the inner-thigh trail friendly.

name: Bodyweight Standing Calf Raise
specificInstructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart on a level floor and rest your fingertips on a fixed support for balance.
Keep your knees softly straight and distribute pressure through the bases of your big and little toes.
Raise your heels to stand tall on the balls of your feet without rolling your ankles outward.
Lower your heels slowly to the floor and pause briefly before the next repetition.
coachTip: Rise like you are peeking over tall grass. The slow landing matters just as much as the view.

name: Side-Lying Quadriceps Stretch
specificInstructions: Lie on one side with your lower knee bent for balance and your head supported comfortably.
Bend the top knee and grasp the ankle behind you, using a strap if reaching it requires twisting.
Keep your knees close and pelvis gently tucked as you guide the heel toward your buttocks until the front thigh stretches mildly.
Hold while breathing, then release the ankle slowly and roll over to repeat on the other side.
coachTip: Keep your tail tucked just a touch. A gentle thigh stretch feels better than pulling your heel as far as it can go.

name: Bodyweight Jump Squat
specificInstructions: Stand with feet approximately shoulder-width apart on a clear, non-slip surface and brace your abdomen.
Lower into a comfortable shallow squat while swinging your arms backward to prepare for the jump.
Push through your feet to extend your hips, knees, and ankles, lifting off vertically without twisting.
Land softly with knees tracking over your toes and bend your hips and knees to absorb the landing before resetting.
coachTip: Quiet paws after every leap. Reset your balance between jumps instead of racing through a noisy landing.

name: Seated Barbell Overhead Press
specificInstructions: Set a near-upright bench inside a rack with safeties, sit with feet planted, and grip the bar slightly wider than your shoulders.
Unrack to the front of your upper chest with your forearms nearly vertical and your abdomen braced.
Press the bar upward in front of your face and then above your shoulders, moving your head only enough to clear its path.
Lower to the front of your upper chest through a comfortable range while keeping your ribs down and your lower back from overextending.
coachTip: Make a tall tower from ribs to hips. The bar goes up; your lower back does not need to join the adventure.

name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
specificInstructions: Sit against a near-upright backrest with feet flat and bring the dumbbells beside your shoulders.
Turn your palms forward or slightly inward and position your elbows a little in front of your torso with wrists above elbows.
Press the dumbbells overhead until your elbows straighten comfortably, allowing your shoulder blades to rotate upward.
Lower the weights beside your shoulders without flaring your ribs or forcing your elbows far behind your body.
coachTip: Give your paws room overhead. A smooth shoulder path beats forcing the dumbbells to touch.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
specificInstructions: Stand with light dumbbells beside your thighs, knees softly bent, and elbows slightly bent.
Raise your upper arms out to your sides and slightly forward of your torso, keeping your wrists in line with your forearms.
Stop around shoulder height with thumbs level or slightly upward rather than pouring your hands downward.
Lower slowly while keeping your torso still and avoiding a shrug to start the next repetition.
coachTip: Spread your wings gently, fox friend. Lighter weights help your shoulders lift without a body swing.

name: Single-Arm Cable Lateral Raise
specificInstructions: Set a single handle on a low pulley and stand sideways with your working arm farther from the cable stack.
Hold the handle across the front of your hips and keep a soft elbow bend with your torso upright.
Lift the working upper arm outward and slightly forward until it approaches shoulder height, keeping your wrist neutral.
Lower the handle slowly toward the opposite hip without leaning away from the machine; finish the set before changing sides.
coachTip: Stay tall like a curious fox. Let the cable stretch the shoulder, not pull you into a sideways lean.

name: Bent-Over Dumbbell Reverse Fly
specificInstructions: Hold light dumbbells, bend your knees slightly, and hinge your hips so your torso angles toward the floor with a neutral back.
Let your hands hang below your chest with palms facing each other and elbows softly bent.
Sweep your upper arms outward until they are roughly level with your torso, keeping the elbow bend nearly unchanged.
Lower the weights slowly beneath your chest without lifting your torso, shrugging, or turning the movement into a row.
coachTip: Open your wings while your body stays still. If your elbows fold into a row, make the weights friendlier.

name: Rope Face Pull
specificInstructions: Attach a rope to a pulley near face height and step back holding one end in each hand with your arms extended.
Set a stable stance and brace your abdomen so the cable cannot pull your ribs forward.
Pull the rope toward your brow while separating its ends beside your face and moving your elbows outward.
Return to straight arms slowly without pushing your head forward or leaning backward to move the weight.
coachTip: Frame your fox ears with the rope ends. Keep your neck long and let your shoulders do the steering.

name: Dumbbell Front Raise
specificInstructions: Stand with light dumbbells in front of your thighs, palms facing you and elbows slightly bent.
Brace your abdomen and lift your arms forward without swinging your hips or leaning back.
Stop with the weights around shoulder height, keeping your wrists straight and your neck relaxed.
Lower the dumbbells slowly to the fronts of your thighs while maintaining the same elbow bend.
coachTip: Lift to the horizon, not the treetops. Shoulder height gives you plenty of work without a big body sway.

name: Machine Shoulder Press
specificInstructions: Adjust the seat so the handles start around shoulder level and your feet can rest securely on the floor.
Sit against the back pad and grip the handles with wrists stacked above your elbows.
Press the handles overhead through a comfortable range while keeping your ribs down and pelvis against the seat.
Lower the handles back toward shoulder height under control without bouncing off the bottom stops.
coachTip: Stay snug against the pad and press tall. The machine guides your paws, while you control the pace.

name: Standing Dumbbell Overhead Press
specificInstructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hold the dumbbells at shoulder level with wrists stacked above your elbows.
Tighten your glutes and abdomen so your rib cage stays centered above your pelvis.
Press the weights overhead without using a knee dip or leaning backward through your lower back.
Lower the dumbbells beside your shoulders slowly while keeping your forearms aligned under them.
coachTip: Stack your ribs over your tail and grow tall. Your legs are a steady base, not a launching spring.

name: Dumbbell Arnold Press
specificInstructions: Sit on a supported bench and hold light dumbbells in front of your shoulders with palms facing your face.
Begin lifting your elbows outward as you rotate your palms forward through a comfortable shoulder range.
Continue pressing overhead without flaring your ribs or forcing your hands farther back than your shoulders allow.
Lower slowly and reverse the rotation until the dumbbells return in front of your shoulders.
coachTip: Turn your paws smoothly, not suddenly. A lighter pair lets your shoulders enjoy the whole winding trail.

name: Machine Lateral Raise
specificInstructions: Set the seat so your shoulders align with the machine pivots and place your upper arms against the pads.
Keep your back supported, feet grounded, and elbows bent as required by the handle position.
Lift your upper arms outward until they reach approximately shoulder height without shrugging toward your ears.
Lower the pads slowly and stop short of dropping the weight stack between repetitions.
coachTip: Let your wings lift while your ears stay relaxed. The pads guide the path; you choose the pace.

name: High Cable Reverse Fly
specificInstructions: Set both pulleys near shoulder-to-head height and hold the opposite handles so the cables cross in front of you.
Stand centered with a stable stance, arms reaching forward and elbows softly bent.
Open your upper arms outward and slightly backward until they align with your torso without lifting your chest or shrugging.
Return your hands forward slowly, keeping the elbow bend nearly unchanged rather than rowing the handles.
coachTip: Unfold your wings without puffing out your ribs. A small, controlled arc can make your rear shoulders work hard.

name: Cable Shoulder External Rotation
specificInstructions: Set a pulley at elbow height and stand sideways with your working arm farther from the stack.
Hold the handle across your abdomen with your elbow bent about 90 degrees and resting near your side.
Rotate your forearm outward away from your abdomen without moving your elbow or turning your torso.
Return the handle slowly across your abdomen through a comfortable range, keeping the resistance light.
coachTip: Tiny turn, patient paws. Keep your elbow near your ribs and choose a load that never makes you twist.

name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
specificInstructions: Stand or sit tall and raise one arm across the front of your chest at roughly shoulder height.
Use your opposite forearm to support above the elbow rather than pressing directly on the elbow joint.
Gently guide the arm closer to your chest while keeping the stretching shoulder down and your torso facing forward.
Breathe through a mild stretch at the back of the shoulder, then release slowly and change arms.
coachTip: Offer your shoulder a gentle fox hug. Keep it away from your ear and skip the extra tug.

name: Barbell Biceps Curl
specificInstructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hold the bar palms-up with hands about shoulder-width apart.
Keep your elbows near the sides of your ribs and your wrists straight as you brace your abdomen.
Bend your elbows to curl the bar toward your shoulders without moving your upper arms forward or swinging your hips.
Lower the bar slowly until your elbows are nearly straight while keeping tension and avoiding a backward trunk lean.
coachTip: Pin your elbows near your den walls. Quiet upper arms turn a curl into honest biceps work.

name: Dumbbell Biceps Curl
specificInstructions: Stand with a dumbbell beside each thigh and your arms extended, palms facing forward or beginning in a neutral grip.
Keep your upper arms beside your torso and rotate your palms upward as you bend your elbows.
Lift the weights toward your shoulders without letting your elbows drift far forward or bending your wrists backward.
Extend your elbows slowly to return the dumbbells beside your thighs, keeping your torso and shoulders still.
coachTip: Show your paws to the sky as you curl. A steady wrist helps your biceps do the carrying.

name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl
specificInstructions: Stand with dumbbells at your sides, palms facing inward and thumbs pointing forward.
Hold your elbows close to your ribs and keep your wrists aligned with your forearms.
Bend your elbows to lift the weights toward the fronts of your shoulders while maintaining the palms-in grip.
Lower the dumbbells slowly without rotating your palms upward or using your hips to start the next curl.
coachTip: Carry two little lanterns with thumbs up. No swinging needed to light up your arms.

name: Standing Cable Biceps Curl
specificInstructions: Attach a short bar to a low pulley and stand facing the stack with an underhand, roughly shoulder-width grip.
Step back just enough to keep tension in the cable and place your upper arms beside your torso.
Curl the bar toward your shoulders by bending your elbows while keeping your shoulders and trunk still.
Extend your elbows slowly without letting your wrists bend or allowing the weight stack to crash down.
coachTip: Keep the cable talking softly. A quiet stack means you are controlling both halves of the curl.

name: Dumbbell Preacher Curl
specificInstructions: Adjust a preacher bench so your upper arm rests fully on the sloped pad with your armpit near its top edge.
Hold a light dumbbell palm-up and keep your shoulder and upper arm resting against the pad.
Bend your elbow to bring the weight toward your shoulder without lifting your upper arm off the support.
Lower slowly until your elbow is nearly straight, stopping short of a forced lockout and avoiding a bounce at the bottom.
coachTip: The pad is your patient training buddy. Keep your upper arm settled and treat the bottom stretch gently.

name: Rope Triceps Pushdown
specificInstructions: Attach a rope to a high pulley and stand facing it with a rope end in each hand and palms facing inward.
Bring your elbows beside your ribs and begin with your forearms angled upward while keeping your torso steady.
Straighten your elbows to move the rope toward your thighs, separating the rope ends slightly as your arms extend.
Let your elbows bend slowly to return without allowing your upper arms to swing forward or your shoulders to shrug.
coachTip: Your elbows are little hinges beside the den door. Keep them parked while your forearms do the swinging.

name: Overhead Rope Triceps Extension
specificInstructions: Attach a rope to a low pulley, face away from the stack, and carefully bring its ends above and behind your head.
Use a staggered stance, brace your abdomen, and hold your upper arms near your ears with elbows pointing upward.
Straighten your elbows to extend the rope overhead while keeping your upper arms and ribs nearly still.
Bend your elbows to lower the rope behind your head through a comfortable stretch without flaring your ribs or pulling your neck forward.
coachTip: Keep your ribs zipped and your ears roomy. Only your elbows need to open and close here.

name: Close-Grip Barbell Bench Press
specificInstructions: Lie on a flat bench inside a rack with safeties or a spotter, and grip the bar about shoulder-width rather than placing your hands together.
Plant your feet, set your shoulder blades against the bench, and unrack the bar above your chest.
Lower toward the lower chest with elbows tracking near your torso and wrists staying stacked above your forearms.
Press upward to straighten your elbows while keeping your buttocks and upper back supported on the bench.
coachTip: Close grip does not mean touching paws. Shoulder-width gives your wrists room while your triceps take the lead.

name: Lying Dumbbell Triceps Extension
specificInstructions: Lie on a flat bench with feet planted and light dumbbells held above your shoulders, palms facing each other.
Keep your upper arms angled slightly toward your head and your wrists straight.
Bend your elbows to lower the weights beside your temples or just beyond your head, keeping the upper-arm position nearly fixed.
Straighten your elbows to return the dumbbells overhead without swinging your shoulders or letting the weights approach your face.
coachTip: Make a safe little path beside your fox ears. Light weights and steady elbows keep this extension tidy.

name: Dumbbell Triceps Kickback
specificInstructions: Hold light dumbbells, soften your knees, and hinge forward with your back neutral and abdomen braced.
Bring your elbows beside your torso so your upper arms are approximately parallel to the floor and your forearms hang downward.
Straighten your elbows to send the weights backward while keeping your upper arms at the same height.
Bend your elbows slowly to return the weights beneath them without swinging your upper arms forward.
coachTip: Your upper arms stay perched like calm fox ears. The forearms flick back; the whole body stays quiet.

name: Incline Dumbbell Biceps Curl
specificInstructions: Sit against a moderately inclined bench with feet planted and let light dumbbells hang beside your torso.
Turn your palms forward and keep your shoulders resting against the pad without forcing your arms backward.
Curl the weights toward your shoulders while keeping your upper arms nearly still and wrists straight.
Lower slowly until your elbows are comfortably extended, avoiding a bounce through the stretched position.
coachTip: Let the bench hold you like a calm den wall. A gentle bottom stretch beats chasing the heaviest curl.

name: Dumbbell Concentration Curl
specificInstructions: Sit with feet apart, lean forward slightly, and rest the back of your working upper arm against your inner thigh.
Hold a dumbbell palm-up with your elbow comfortably extended and your free hand bracing the other thigh.
Curl the weight toward your shoulder without lifting your upper arm from your thigh or bending your wrist.
Lower slowly to the starting range, then complete the set before switching arms.
coachTip: One paw gets the spotlight. Keep your thigh support steady and give every curl your full fox focus.

name: EZ-Bar Biceps Curl
specificInstructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and grip the angled sections of an EZ bar with palms facing mostly upward.
Keep your elbows beside your ribs and your wrists aligned naturally with the bar bends.
Bend your elbows to bring the bar toward your shoulders without swinging your hips or lifting your upper arms.
Lower the bar slowly until your elbows are nearly straight while keeping your shoulders relaxed.
coachTip: Find the bends that feel friendly to your paws. A comfortable wrist helps you keep the curl smooth.

name: Reverse Barbell Curl
specificInstructions: Hold a light barbell with an overhand grip about shoulder-width apart and let it rest in front of your thighs.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and wrists straight rather than allowing your knuckles to drop.
Curl the bar upward by bending your elbows while maintaining the palms-down grip.
Lower slowly until your elbows are nearly straight without swinging your torso to restart the movement.
coachTip: Knuckles up and paws steady. This grip asks more of your forearms, so a lighter bar is a smart choice.

name: Single-Arm Cable Triceps Pushdown
specificInstructions: Attach one handle to a high pulley and stand facing the stack with the handle held beside your chest.
Set your working elbow beside your ribs and keep your shoulder down with your torso still.
Straighten your elbow to move the handle toward the outside of your thigh without pushing your upper arm backward.
Bend your elbow slowly to return the handle upward while keeping the elbow position fixed.
coachTip: One little hinge does the job. Park your elbow and let the forearm travel smoothly down the trail.

name: Diamond Push-Up
specificInstructions: Start in a high plank with hands close together beneath your chest, forming a loose diamond with thumbs and index fingers if comfortable.
Brace your abdomen and glutes while keeping your shoulders centered over your hand support.
Bend your elbows backward near your torso to lower your chest toward your hands without letting your hips sag.
Press through your palms to straighten your arms; widen your hands slightly or elevate them if the close position strains your wrists.
coachTip: Your diamond can be a little wider. Happy wrists and a straight fox silhouette matter more than touching fingertips.

name: Seated Overhead Dumbbell Triceps Extension
specificInstructions: Sit upright with feet planted and use both hands to support one dumbbell securely above your head.
Keep your upper arms near your ears and brace your abdomen to prevent your ribs from flaring.
Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head through a comfortable shoulder and elbow range.
Straighten your elbows to lift the weight overhead without swinging your upper arms or leaning back.
coachTip: Keep your ribs tucked while your paws reach tall. A secure grip and a light start make this a friendly overhead trail.

name: Overhead Triceps Stretch
specificInstructions: Sit or stand tall and raise one arm overhead before bending that elbow so your hand reaches behind your upper back.
Rest the other hand lightly above the bent elbow without pressing on the elbow joint itself.
Keep your ribs down and guide the upper arm gently backward only until the back of your arm stretches mildly.
Hold with slow breaths, then release the support and lower your arm before switching sides.
coachTip: A gentle reach behind your fox ears is enough. Keep breathing and let the stretch stay soft.

name: Dead Bug
specificInstructions: Lie on your back with arms pointing toward the ceiling and hips and knees bent approximately 90 degrees.
Exhale to gently draw your ribs down and keep your lower back from arching away from the floor.
Reach one arm behind you and extend the opposite leg toward the floor only as far as you can maintain your trunk position.
Bring the arm and leg back above your torso, then alternate sides slowly while continuing to breathe.
coachTip: Move your paws slowly like a sleepy fox stretch. A shorter reach with a steady back is a winning rep.

name: Reverse Crunch
specificInstructions: Lie on your back with arms resting beside you and hips and knees bent so your thighs point upward.
Exhale and curl your pelvis toward your ribs, lifting your tailbone a few centimeters from the floor.
Keep your knees bent and avoid throwing your legs toward your face or pressing hard through your hands.
Lower your pelvis slowly back to the mat, stopping before momentum rolls you into the next repetition.
coachTip: Curl your tail, do not launch your legs. A tiny controlled lift can give your abs a big challenge.

name: Floor Crunch
specificInstructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat; rest your fingertips lightly beside your head without interlacing behind your neck.
Keep a small comfortable gap between your chin and chest and exhale as you bring your ribs toward your pelvis.
Lift your shoulder blades slightly off the floor without sitting all the way up or pulling your head forward.
Lower your upper back to the floor slowly while keeping your feet relaxed and your neck aligned.
coachTip: Think ribs toward hips, fox friend. Your paws are passengers beside your head, not a neck-pulling team.

name: Side Plank
specificInstructions: Lie on one side with your elbow directly under your shoulder, forearm on the floor, and legs extended with feet stacked or staggered.
Press through your forearm and the sides of your feet to lift your hips until your head, ribs, pelvis, and ankles form a line.
Keep your pelvis facing forward rather than rolling backward, and breathe steadily while maintaining space between your shoulder and ear.
Lower your hips under control and switch sides; bend your knees and support from them if you cannot hold the straight-leg version.
coachTip: Build a little side bridge and keep your tail from drooping. Short, steady holds count.

name: Band Pallof Press
specificInstructions: Secure a resistance band at chest height, stand sideways to the anchor, and hold the band with both hands at your sternum.
Step away until the band is taut, set your feet shoulder-width apart, and soften your knees.
Press your hands straight forward from your chest while resisting the band pulling your shoulders or pelvis toward the anchor.
Pause briefly with arms extended, return your hands to your chest, and complete the set before turning to face the opposite direction.
coachTip: Be the fox that will not twist in the breeze. If the band turns you, take one small step closer.

name: Plank Shoulder Tap
specificInstructions: Start in a high plank with hands under your shoulders, legs extended, and feet a little wider than hip-width.
Brace your abdomen and glutes while pressing evenly through both palms to keep your torso level.
Shift your weight slightly into one hand and lift the other hand to touch the opposite shoulder without letting your hips rotate.
Replace the hand beneath your shoulder and alternate sides slowly; widen your feet or elevate your hands if you cannot stay steady.
coachTip: Balance an imaginary acorn on your back. Slow taps keep that little treasure from rolling away.

name: Mountain Climber
specificInstructions: Place your hands directly below your shoulders in a high plank, with legs extended and abdomen braced.
Bring one knee toward your chest without rounding your shoulders forward or lifting your hips sharply.
Return that foot behind you and draw the opposite knee forward, keeping your weight supported through your hands and toes.
Continue alternating at a pace that lets your hips stay level; slow to individual steps if your trunk begins to bounce.
coachTip: Quick paws are optional; steady hips are the goal. Find a climbing pace your whole body can control.

name: Jumping Jack
specificInstructions: Stand with feet together or comfortably close, arms beside your body, and knees softly bent.
Hop your feet outward while sweeping your arms sideways and upward through a comfortable shoulder range.
Land quietly with knees tracking over your feet, then hop your feet inward as your arms return to your sides.
Repeat rhythmically while breathing; use alternating side steps instead of jumps when you want a lower-impact version.
coachTip: Land like a fox sneaking past a sleeping owl. Soft paws make the rhythm smoother.

name: Jump Rope
specificInstructions: Hold the rope handles beside your hips with elbows close to your ribs and the rope resting behind your heels.
Turn the rope mainly with small wrist circles while keeping your shoulders relaxed and your gaze forward.
Hop just high enough for the rope to pass under your feet, landing softly through your forefeet with knees slightly bent.
Maintain small repeated hops and steady breathing; stop and reset when the rope catches rather than rushing the next jump.
coachTip: Small hops save fox energy. Let your wrists spin the rope while your shoulders enjoy the ride.

name: Stationary Bike
specificInstructions: Adjust the saddle so your knee remains slightly bent when the pedal reaches its lowest point, and secure your feet on the pedals.
Set the handlebars to a comfortable reach that lets your elbows stay soft and your shoulders relaxed.
Begin with light resistance and pedal in smooth circles while keeping your hips level on the saddle.
Increase resistance gradually to a pace where you can still speak in sentences, then finish with a slower easy pedal before stopping.
coachTip: Spin a trail you can chat through. Smooth circles and a comfy saddle make a happy fox ride.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
specificInstructions: Grasp a secure overhead bar and hang with your legs together, keeping your shoulders engaged rather than swinging freely.
Brace your abdomen and lift your legs forward toward hip height with knees softly straight.
Gently curl your pelvis upward near the top instead of only hinging through your hips.
Lower slowly until your legs hang below you and pause to stop any swing; use bent knees when straight legs are too demanding.
coachTip: No swinging tail on this branch. Shorter, still repetitions are stronger than a big momentum-powered kick.

name: Bodyweight Russian Twist
specificInstructions: Sit with knees bent and heels resting on the floor, then lean back slightly while keeping your chest lifted.
Hold your hands together in front of your sternum and brace your abdomen to maintain the trunk angle.
Turn your ribs and shoulders a small distance to one side while keeping your pelvis as steady as possible.
Return through center and rotate to the other side slowly without throwing your arms or rounding your lower back.
coachTip: Turn your chest, not just your paws. Heels down and a small smooth twist keep you in control.

name: Weighted Forearm Plank
specificInstructions: First establish a steady forearm plank with elbows under shoulders, toes on the floor, and body aligned from head to heels.
Have a partner place a light plate across your upper-to-mid back, away from your neck and lower back.
Brace your abdomen and glutes while breathing normally and keeping your hips from sagging or rising.
Ask your partner to remove the plate before lowering your knees; shorten the hold if your back position changes.
coachTip: Earn the quiet plank before adding an acorn. A light plate and a helpful partner keep this challenge controlled.

name: Burpee
specificInstructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, bend your knees and hips, and place your palms on the floor in front of your feet.
Step or hop your feet back into a stable high plank, keeping your ribs and pelvis aligned.
Lower your chest with a controlled push-up and press back up, then bring your feet forward near your hands.
Stand and make a small vertical jump, landing softly before resetting; omit the push-up or jump when you need a lower-impact version.
coachTip: One tidy step at a time beats a frantic fox scramble. You can skip the leap and still earn a great round.

name: Elliptical Cross-Trainer
specificInstructions: Hold the fixed handles while stepping onto the stationary pedals and center each foot on its platform.
Begin pedaling slowly with your torso upright and knees tracking in the direction of your toes.
Choose a light resistance and move the handles naturally without hanging your body weight on them.
Maintain smooth strides at a pace that allows conversation, then slow the pedals completely before stepping off.
coachTip: Glide along the trail with a tall chest. The handles help with rhythm, not with holding up your whole fox self.

name: Incline Treadmill Walk
specificInstructions: Attach the treadmill safety clip and begin walking at a slow speed before raising the incline.
Increase the incline gradually while keeping your steps short enough to land beneath your body.
Walk upright with a slight whole-body lean from the ankles rather than bending at the waist or hanging on the rails.
Reduce the incline and speed for a short cooldown, then stop the belt fully before stepping off.
coachTip: Pick a hill you can walk proudly. If you need to cling to the rails, make the slope a little friendlier.
